title: SER timestamp arithmetic narrows to 32-bit long on Windows
summary: Timestamp arithmetic uses long, which is 32 bits on Windows LLP64. The cast first narrows epoch seconds to long; subsequent multiplication by 10000000L can overflow signed long. The timezone multiplication likewise uses 32-bit long. The uint64_t serializer cannot repair prior truncation/overflow. Synthetic Unix seconds 1793563200 require 639291636000000000 ticks. Use explicit 64-bit epoch/tick and signed timezone arithmetic; assert serialized timestamps. Source-contract confirmed; Windows execution unavailable.
